correctness.rationale: For the repaired short-window claim, Gaussian regression gives the conditional quadratic residual (b^T M^-1 W)^2-b^T M^-1 b. This times the pair density is twice its first covariance derivative along M+tbb^T. Differentiating the arccos crossing probability gives the stated covariance with sign, factor of two, and denominator; dominated differentiation is valid for 0<=rho<1. Summing over coordinates of HX centers at the sample mean, and rewriting the numerator using the difference of adjacent centered columns gives the polynomial expression. I independently built nHa_i coefficientwise by distance counts and verified the five full polynomial factorizations and exact Bernstein minima (1, 1, 5/2, 23/20, 11/56) using integer convolution and rational arithmetic. The new standard-library /workspace/repairs/5/verify_gaussian.py was inspected and successfully run; it proves the coefficient certificates only, not anything about infinitely many n. Positivity of each Bernstein polynomial on [0,1], and of the remaining factors and denominator on [0,1), establishes the repaired claim including rho=0 and excluding the degenerate endpoint. The already documented n>=7 signs are explicitly cited rather than presented as new. The original proof is mathematically sound: expanding the centered correction at 1/2 gives the stated half-parameter numerator; the endpoint coefficient is the sum of 4i(n-i)/n, and the large-window limit follows from the geometric raw-energy sum and the bounded column sums. The delivered repair is a narrowed claim, not a correctness reversal.

value.rationale: The cutoff is not an arbitrary collection of dimensions: the known sign theorem starts at seven, and its sharpness requires ruling out every smaller n over a continuous range of correlations. In particular the six-observation case has mixed power coefficients and a much smaller positive minimum Bernstein coefficient, so selected evaluations would not settle it. The repaired exact exclusion answers the natural minimum-window question for a joint statistic that differs in sign from the corresponding raw-energy statistic. No additional significance is assigned to recomputing the covered large-window identity or signs.
